description.narrative: The program is part of a long-term partnership between the Asian Development Bank (ADB) and the Government of the Philippines to increase financial inclusion by (i) strengthening the institutional and policy environment, (ii) improving financial infrastructure, and (iii) increasing the capacity and reach of financial service providers. Under subprogram 3, the government will build on achievements under subprograms 1 and 2 by implementing key reforms, including (i) supporting coronavirus disease (COVID-19) recovery efforts by leveraging the national identity system to expand financial inclusion; (ii) expanding the digital payment ecosystem; (iii) increasing the capacity of financial service providers through digital transformation; (iv) reducing inequalities in women's access to finance and promoting women's economic empowerment; and (v) implementing financial enhancements to respond to the impact of climate change, particularly for the country's most vulnerable populations.

1.1. The government submitted proposed legislation to Congress to develop a foundational NIDS with an identification card to provide for a range of benefits and government services and improve access to finance. (IA: PSA)
1.10. The government submitted legislation to Congress to establish a modern secured transactions system and the creation of a centralized, online national collateral registry. (IA: DOJ)

1.11. The government submitted a draft Executive Order to bring the state financed guarantee funds (e.g., PhilEXIM, Agriculture Guarantee Fund Pool, Small Business and Guarantee Finance Corporation (or SB Corporation), Industrial Guarantee and Loan Fund and the Home Guaranty Corporation together under one governing entity to increase efficiencies and expand access to finance. (IA: PhilGuarantee)

1.12. The government established the MNRC as a microfinance standard setting body. The MNRC (i) adopted governance performance standards for MF-NGOs (including gender diversity on the board), and (ii) prescribed a standard chart of accounts for accredited MF-NGOs. (IA: SEC) (IA: BSP, DTI)

1.13. The BSP approved an innovative pilot for a rural bank to migrate its physical core banking system to a cloud- based system to showcase how digital innovation can enable banks to manage operations and serve clients more effectively. (IA: BSP)

1.14. The government submitted legislation to Congress to establish a strong legal and policy framework for the development of Islamic finance in the country. This framework also ensures an environment of increased consumer awareness and capacity building of providers on Islamic finance. (IA: BSP)
1.2. The government allocated $40 million (equivalent) through the 2018 GAA for NIDS development. (IA: PSA)

1.3. The BSP introduced a policy framework to promote AVCF. Under this framework, BSP- supervised financial institutions participating in AVCF would be able to address risks associated with lending to the agriculture sector by shifting the focus of lending from individual farmers to the whole value chain. (IA: BSP)

1.4. The Insurance Commission issued regulatory frameworks for microinsurance that: (i) allowed microinsurance providers to further develop microinsurance products on agriculture and health; (ii) enhanced functions of licensed microinsurance general agents, brokers, Cooperative Insurance Societies, and Mutual Benefit Associations to increase the outreach of microinsurance; (iii) defined acceptable distribution channels and permissible functions to further increase outreach; and (iv) enhanced performance indicators and standards for microinsurance providers. (IA: IC)
1.5. Legislation was enacted for an annual Economic and Financial Literacy Week to increase financial literacy awareness among the public and policymakers. (IA: BSP)

1.6. The BSP issued a policy framework to promote the establishment of a safe, efficient, and interoperable national retail payment system (NRPS) that allows (i) transfer funds from one bank or financial service provider to another through transaction accounts, and (ii) any qualified financial service provider to participate on a level playing field. The goal is to drive usage of electronic payments from the current 1% to 20% by 2020 and promote a digital finance ecosystem that can facilitate the deployment of a wide range of affordable financial products and services. (IA: BSP)

1.7. The BSP collaborated with the banking and payments industry to establish two ACHs for (i) batched electronic fund transfer credit that could be used to replace checks, and (ii) real time low value push that enables low value electronic fund transfers. (IA: BSP)

1.8. To extend the reach of traditional branches, the BSP issued new guidelines for banks allowing them to use third party cash agents as a cost-efficient service delivery channel. Among others, the guidelines allow the cash agents to collect deposits, disperse cash, and provide other financial services on behalf of banks. (IA: BSP)

1.9. The government, through the SEC, increased the number of people with a formal financial credit history by (i) requiring financing companies to provide their 3-year historical and current credit data to the CIC, and (ii) enabling MF-NGOs to submit credit data to the CIC with the assistance of the MIDAS (a credit bureau for microfinance NGOs). (IA: SEC)

2.1. To institutionalize PhilSys, the government: (i) issued IRR which include provisions to facilitate registration of children, senior citizens, and persons with disabilities; and (ii) approved a four-year implementation road map on the foundational ID system and its role in increasing financial inclusion through streamlined identity verification for financial account opening, among others. (IA: PSA)
2.10. To increase coverage of the credit reporting system, the SEC and CDA required cooperatives and MF NGO s to submit sex-disaggregated credit data to the CIC. (IA: SEC)

2.11. To improve access to credit, following approval of R.A. No. 11057 (Personal Property Security Act) in August 2018, the government adopted rules for the online national movable collateral registry through the issuance of IRR in October 2019. (IA: DOJ)

2.12. To strengthen credit enhancement mechanisms, the government formulated an action plan that included: (i) merger and transfer of guarantee functions, programs, and funds into one entity, the PhilGuarantee (formerly PhilEXIM); (ii) review of guarantee policies, pricing structure, and risk management; (iii) establishment of a sound governance structure and internal control framework to safeguard its sustainability, integrity, and efficiency; (iv) infusion of capital, as part of its capital build-up plan; and (v) issuance of Circular 1-2019 approving the Restructuring Plan of PhilGuarantee. (IA: PhilGuarantee)

2.13. To strengthen regulatory oversight over MF NGOs, the MNRC (i) adapted internal SEC: IT systems to provide for collection of sex disaggregated data on boards of trustees, management, personnel, and client borrowers of MF-NGOs; (ii) designed a training program to build capacity of the MNRC and MF-NGOs to comply with MNRC accreditation and CIC requirements, starting with the development of a supervision manual for MF-NGOs with pilot testing and onsite training; and (iii) issued revised guidelines for accreditation of MF NGOs in December 2018. As of March 2020, 30 MF-NGOs have been accredited with 100% having female representation on their boards. (IA: SEC)

2.14. To support innovative and inclusive financial technology solutions, the BSP issued licenses to financial technology companies and financial institutions to expand the range and reach of financial services. (IA: BSP)

2.15. To broaden the range of financial products to include Islamic finance, Congress enacted the Islamic Banking law, and the BSP; (i) conducted awareness raising and capacity-building campaigns; and (ii) issued regulations outlining a framework for licensing of Islamic banks and Islamic banking windows by existing banks, and supporting government's issuance of sukuk or sharia compliant bonds. (IA: BSP)

2.2. To ensure effective implementation of PhilSys, the government allocated: (i) ₱2 billion ($40 million equivalent) through the 2019 GAA for the purchase of 5,000 registration kits and budget for the Automated Biometric Identification System provider; (ii) ₱2 billion ($40 million equivalent) through the 2020 GAA for the ongoing implementation of the PhilSys, including the procurement of the Systems Integrator, fixed and mobile registration centers costs, card production costs, compensation for staff requirements; and (iii) ₱1 billion ($20 million equivalent) from 2020 unprogrammed funds for the ongoing implementation of the PhilSys. (IA: PSA)

2.3. To promote the financial inclusion of agricultural enterprises, with endorsement from the NSFI Steering Committee, the BSP supported implementation of the pilot AVCF program for rural and thrift banks, which fosters value chain finance lending to agriculture enterprises, including women-owned enterprises. (IA: BSP)

2.4. To expand the availability and diversity of insurance products, the government, through the Insurance Commission: (i) formulated registration guidelines to support implementation of distribution channels that include women-owned enterprises to increase the number and diversity of insurance products; and (ii) supported a test and learn approach to implementing a pilot public private partnership for agriculture insurance. (IA: IC)

2.5. To increase nationwide financial literacy, the BSP implemented an enhanced Economic and Financial Learning Program informed by: (i) a Financial Education Stocktaking Study; and (ii) a Financial Inclusion Survey including information related to gender, age, access to financial services such as savings and credit, and knowledge on basic financial concepts (51% of respondents were female). (IA: BSP)

2.6. To strengthen financial consumer protection mechanisms, the BSP: (i) amended existing regulations on financial consumer protection to promote broad and convenient access to high quality financial services and consider the interest of the public, including vulnerable groups such as the low-income earners and persons with disability; (ii) drafted introduction of FCPA; and (iii) developed a prototype Chatbot using artificial intelligence and natural language processing to provide the public with a more accessible and efficient means to engage the BSP on financial consumer concerns. (IA: BSP)

2.7. To promote women's financial inclusion, the BSP as chair of the NSFI Steering Committee: (i) endorsed the inclusion of the PCW as a full member of the committee; and (ii) conducted the first national stakeholder workshop, with participation of PCW as a member of the project steering committee, on the design of the first comprehensive, national MSME survey with a gender focus, complementing the enterprise survey conducted by the DOF in collaboration with ADB investigating the impact of COVID-19 on Philippine MSMEs, including female owned or led enterprises. (IA: BSP)

2.8. The share of digital transactions increased from 8% in 2013 to 20% in 2019 by value and from 1% in 2013 to 8% in 2019 by volume. To achieve this, the BSP: (i) issued amendments to regulations on Electronic Banking Services; (ii) introduced a National QR Code Standard for payments necessary for ensuring interoperability of QR-enabled payment and financial services; (iii) formulated a partnership with DOLE to promote payment of salaries through formal accounts and digitizing payments in public transportation; and (iv) pilot tested the government's BTMS that enables direct transfer of payments to suppliers through PESONet integration. (IA: BSP, DOLE, DBM)

2.9. To extend the reach of traditional branches, the BSP: (i) issued policies to support implementation of cash agents and guidelines for usage of branch-lites, and established standards for the conduct of these activities; and (ii) issued rules and regulations to support payment channels for the government's social protection programs including the 4Ps program (for which 85.3% of beneficiaries are women), and other cash transfer programs, particularly in rural areas. (IA: BSP, DSWD)

3.1. The government implemented PhilSys by: (i) enrolling 77.9 million persons by 31 March 2023, generating sex disaggregated identity data; and (ii) the opening of 8.4 million additional transaction accounts as of 31 December 2022 through a partnership with Land Bank of the Philippines; and (iii) operationalizing linkages within the financial sector and PhilSys with the BSP through: (a) the issuance on 7 June 2021 Memorandum 2021-035 on the use of the Philippine Identification System (PhilSys) ID (PhilID) for customer identification and verification for all financial institutions supervised by the BSP; (b) the issuance on 21 October 2021 of regulations requiring all BSP-supervised financial institutions to use the PhilID as sufficient proof of identity; (c) the issuance of Memorandum No. 2022-44 on 14 October 2022 on the use and acceptance of the PhilSys digital ID and printed e-Philippine Identification (ePhilID); and (d) the issuance on 30 March 2023 of guidelines for supervised financial institutions to help onboard clients using PhilSys which enabled the eKYC process. (IA: BSP, PSA)

3.10. The government: (i) through the BSP, issued Memorandum No. 2021-031 to all banks with cash agent operations on 28 May 2021, with immediate effect, advising banks to ensure that customers are adequately informed and protected when transacting with their cash agents, and developed tailored videos to increase awareness of transaction accounts and cash agents; and (ii) through the DSWD, which transitioned to the use of transaction accounts (deposit accounts, e-money, or e wallets) through banks accredited and managed by the government, for the distribution of cash grants under the government's social protection programs. (IA: BSP, DSWD)

3.11. The SEC: (i) accredited 27 MF-NGOs, with 23 reporting through MIDAS to the CIC, submitting sex disaggregated and other credit data as mandated by law; and (ii) operationalized linkages to PhilSys and the CIC on 11 April 2022 by requiring submitting entities to use the PCN as secondary identification. (IA: SEC)

3.12. The LRA (i) implemented Circular No. 11-2021 on Implementing Guidelines on the Use of the PPSR for the Creation of User Accounts to Access the PPSR effective 15 March 2021; (ii) implemented Circular No. 09-2022 on Implementing Guidelines for the Registering of Notices on Security Interest Involving Personal Property, effective 13 March 2022 to facilitate use of the registry; and (iii) adopted the inclusion of gender as a field to be accomplished in the electronic registry, the use of the national definition of women owned and women led enterprises, and updated the manual on the use of the registry to reflect the additional field on gender. (IA: DOJ)

3.13. PhilGuarantee: (i) implemented post-merger measures to significantly improve its cost-to-income position; and (ii) increased support in priority sectors with MSME guarantees increasing by 110% from 2020 to 2022, with collection of data disaggregated by sex, industry, and region. (IA: PhilGuarantee)

3.14. The MNRC: (i) issued updated guidelines on 24 November 2021 for the accreditation of MF-NGOs for the period 2022 to 2025 including an assessment of financial performance, social performance, and good governance (which includes collection of sex-disaggregated data); and (ii) commenced in 2020 annual supervisory examinations (in accordance with R.A. 10693 establishing the MNRC) through online systems and desk audits of at least 30% of the accredited MF NGOs. (IA: SEC)

3.15. The BSP launched and implemented a comprehensive reform and capacity development program for rural banks through: (i) the issuance on 5 May 2022 of Memorandum No. M 2022-024 with detailed guidelines on the Implementation of the Rural Bank Strengthening Program; (ii) the issuance on 24 August 2022 of BSP Circular No. 1151 amending the minimum capitalization requirements for rural banks and introducing the Rural Bank Strengthening Program, a comprehensive training program on risk management and capacity development grants to enhance the operations, capacity, and competitiveness of rural banks; (iii) conduct of a credit risk management course for rural banks from 28 November to 5 December 2022; and (iv) the inception of a matching grant financial technology fund for rural banks in February 2023. (IA: BSP)

3.16. The government: (i) through the BSP: (a) issued and implemented the Regulatory Sandbox Framework through Circular No. 1153 on 5 September 2022 to test new business models, facilitate the adoption of innovative financial technology solutions, and assess potential risks; and (b) applied supervisory technology solutions to streamline its functions to make regulatory reporting of supervised financial institutions easier and more efficient; and (ii) through DTI, implemented the development of a range of financial technology innovations including those that specifically address women-led unserved or underserved MSMEs due to constraints in access to financial services from formal financial institutions. (IA: BSP, DTI)

3.17. The BSP: (i) issued on 26 April 2022 a joint circular and a memorandum of agreement with the DOF, the National Commission on Muslim Filipinos, and the Bangsamoro Government to create the Shari'ah Supervisory Board in Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao to promote Islamic finance and Islamic banking and finance in the region; and (ii) implemented a capacity building program on Islamic banking for over 700 representatives (with 62% women) of regulatory agencies, the banking industry, and other stakeholders. (IA: BSP)

3.2. The government allocated: (i) ₱4.3 billion through the 2021 GAA and an additional ₱9.9 billion authorized by the President to accelerate step one of the PhilSys enrollment process; and (ii) ₱4.8 billion through the 2022 GAA for PhilSys implementation and to cover the development of a digital version of the ID with a downloadable mobile application and the launch of an authentication platform. (IA: PSA)

3.3. The BSP: (i) issued on 4 November 2022 the IRR for R.A. No. 11901, known as The Agriculture, Fisheries and Rural Development Financing Enhancement Act of 2022, to encourage electronic platforms to provide supply chain financing among actors in the agriculture value chain; (ii) implemented a pilot AVCF program with six rural and thrift banks from 2020 to 2022; (iii) based on the pilot, rolled out a toolkit in February 2023 which includes guidelines on gender-based analysis to identify constraints that should be considered in developing AVCF loan proposals; and (iv) commenced implementation of a training program for other rural and thrift banks on 27 February 2023. (IA: BSP)

3.4. The Insurance Commission: (i) issued, with immediate effect, Circular Letter No. 2023 10 on 15 March 2023 mandating the collection of sex disaggregated microinsurance data to help identify gender differentiated outputs and impacts of microinsurance; (ii) issued Insurance Memorandum Circular No. 2023 01 on 12 March 2023 on market conduct to safeguard the rights and interests of the insuring public, including life, non-life, pre-need, and HMO customers supporting the new FCPA; (iii) issued guidelines, effective as of 15 October 2021, on the adoption of a regulatory sandbox framework for piloting agriculture insurance, including requirements for insurance companies to develop comprehensive and gender-sensitive insurance and digital literacy tailored to the needs of potential male and female clients; and (iv) executed the first national pilot public-private partnership in agriculture insurance which became effective 2 February 2022 pursuant to Circular Letter No. 2021-60. (IA: IC)

3.5. The BSP: (i) expanded the Economic and Financial Learning Program through the implementation of additional strategic partnership programs with key public and private sector stakeholders to deepen financial education, digital financial literacy and instill sound personal finance practices in Filipinos, including marginalized women, men, and their families, through a range of approaches to training delivery; (ii) implemented the Department of Education Financial Education Policy, approved 3 June 2021 to provide efficient and effective integration of financial education concepts within the K to 12 curriculum to reach over 900,000 Department of Education personnel and 28 million learners; and (iii) through the updated NSFI, implemented a monitoring and evaluation framework to measure progress of financial literacy activities. (IA: BSP)

3.6. Financial consumer protection was strengthened as: (i) Congress enacted the FCPA and signed it into law on 6 May 2022, which mandates that financial persons, among others, observe fair and respectful treatment of clients regardless of race, age, financial capacity, ethnicity, origin, gender, disability, health conditions, sexual orientation, religious affiliation, or political affiliation; (ii) the BSP implemented regulations on the FCPA with the issuance of Circular No. 1169 Rules of Procedure for the Consumer Assistance Mechanism, Mediation, and Adjudication of Cases in the BSP on 24 March 2023; and (iii) the BSP implemented the chatbot to provide the public with a more accessible and efficient means to engage with the BSP on financial consumer concerns. (IA: BSP)

3.7. The BSP implemented the first phase of the updated NSFI 2022- 2028, approved in January 2022, which includes an action plan with gender-focused targets and a robust monitoring and evaluation framework, developed with inputs from the first national MSME demand survey with a focus on women and women-owned enterprises and recommendations on policy and financial support measures to rescue affected MSMEs in light of COVID-19, especially targeting women-owned MSMEs. (IA: BSP)

3.8. The government advanced women's financial inclusion through: (i) the DTI MSME Development Council endorsing a national definition of women owned and women-led businesses to be used across government effective 29 December 2022; and (ii) the Government Procurement Policy Board adopting Resolution No. 01-202 with guidelines for gender-responsive procurement policies which became effective on 21 March 2023. (IA: DBM, DTI)

3.9. The government upgraded the retail payments system through: (i) BSP collection and reporting of sex-disaggregated data on payments through the BSP bi annual financial inclusion survey which helped identify differences in use patterns and informed delivery interventions outlined in the updated NSFI; (ii) the BSP implementing measures to scale up the adoption of the National QR Code Standard through the issuance of Memorandum No. 2023-005 on 23 February 2023 mandating payment service providers to adopt the National QR Code Standard based on the implementation of BSP Circular No. 1055 on the Adoption of a National Quick QR Standard (QR Ph) based on a QR Ph P2M facility piloted among select banks to extend the payment use case of QR Ph enabling digital payments between customers and merchants; (iii) the government issuing Labor Advisory No. 26, Series of 2020 in August 2020 to promote the payment of salaries through formal accounts and digitizing payments on public transportation;c and (iv) the government mainstreaming BTMS through the issuance of LTFRB Memorandum Circular No. 2020-018 to enable the direct transfer of payments to suppliers through PESONet integration. (IA: BSP, DOLE, DBM)

description.narrative:
Policy 1: Institutional and policy environment for financial inclusion strengthened. NA
Action 2: To ensure effective implementation of PhilSys, the government allocated: (i) ₱2 billion ($40 million equivalent) through the 2019 GAA for the purchase of 5,000 registration kits and budget for the Automated Biometric Identification System provider; (ii) ₱2 billion ($40 million equivalent) through the 2020 GAA for the ongoing implementation of the PhilSys, including the procurement of the Systems Integrator, fixed and mobile registration centers costs, card production costs, compensation for staff requirements; and (iii) ₱1 billion ($20 million equivalent) from 2020 unprogrammed funds for the ongoing implementation of the PhilSys. (IA: PSA) Target date: 2020-04-30
Action 3: To promote the financial inclusion of agricultural enterprises, with endorsement from the NSFI Steering Committee, the BSP supported implementation of the pilot AVCF program for rural and thrift banks, which fosters value chain finance lending to agriculture enterprises, including women-owned enterprises. (IA: BSP) Target date: 2020-04-30
Action 4: To expand the availability and diversity of insurance products, the government, through the Insurance Commission: (i) formulated registration guidelines to support implementation of distribution channels that include women-owned enterprises to increase the number and diversity of insurance products; and (ii) supported a test and learn approach to implementing a pilot public private partnership for agriculture insurance. (IA: IC) Target date: 2020-04-30
Action 5: To increase nationwide financial literacy, the BSP implemented an enhanced Economic and Financial Learning Program informed by: (i) a Financial Education Stocktaking Study; and (ii) a Financial Inclusion Survey including information related to gender, age, access to financial services such as savings and credit, and knowledge on basic financial concepts (51% of respondents were female). (IA: BSP) Target date: 2020-04-30
Action 6: To strengthen financial consumer protection mechanisms, the BSP: (i) amended existing regulations on financial consumer protection to promote broad and convenient access to high quality financial services and consider the interest of the public, including vulnerable groups such as the low-income earners and persons with disability; (ii) drafted introduction of FCPA; and (iii) developed a prototype Chatbot using artificial intelligence and natural language processing to provide the public with a more accessible and efficient means to engage the BSP on financial consumer concerns. (IA: BSP) Target date: 2020-04-30
Action 7: To promote women's financial inclusion, the BSP as chair of the NSFI Steering Committee: (i) endorsed the inclusion of the PCW as a full member of the committee; and (ii) conducted the first national stakeholder workshop, with participation of PCW as a member of the project steering committee, on the design of the first comprehensive, national MSME survey with a gender focus, complementing the enterprise survey conducted by the DOF in collaboration with ADB investigating the impact of COVID-19 on Philippine MSMEs, including female owned or led enterprises. (IA: BSP) Target date: 2020-04-30
Action 1: The government implemented PhilSys by: (i) enrolling 77.9 million persons by 31 March 2023, generating sex disaggregated identity data; and (ii) the opening of 8.4 million additional transaction accounts as of 31 December 2022 through a partnership with Land Bank of the Philippines; and (iii) operationalizing linkages within the financial sector and PhilSys with the BSP through: (a) the issuance on 7 June 2021 Memorandum 2021-035 on the use of the Philippine Identification System (PhilSys) ID (PhilID) for customer identification and verification for all financial institutions supervised by the BSP; (b) the issuance on 21 October 2021 of regulations requiring all BSP-supervised financial institutions to use the PhilID as sufficient proof of identity; (c) the issuance of Memorandum No. 2022-44 on 14 October 2022 on the use and acceptance of the PhilSys digital ID and printed e-Philippine Identification (ePhilID); and (d) the issuance on 30 March 2023 of guidelines for supervised financial institutions to help onboard clients using PhilSys which enabled the eKYC process. (IA: BSP, PSA) Target date: 2023-03-31

Action 2: The BSP launched and implemented a comprehensive reform and capacity development program for rural banks through: (i) the issuance on 5 May 2022 of Memorandum No. M 2022-024 with detailed guidelines on the Implementation of the Rural Bank Strengthening Program; (ii) the issuance on 24 August 2022 of BSP Circular No. 1151 amending the minimum capitalization requirements for rural banks and introducing the Rural Bank Strengthening Program, a comprehensive training program on risk management and capacity development grants to enhance the operations, capacity, and competitiveness of rural banks; (iii) conduct of a credit risk management course for rural banks from 28 November to 5 December 2022; and (iv) the inception of a matching grant financial technology fund for rural banks in February 2023. (IA: BSP) Target date: 2023-03-31
Action 3: The government: (i) through the BSP: (a) issued and implemented the Regulatory Sandbox Framework through Circular No. 1153 on 5 September 2022 to test new business models, facilitate the adoption of innovative financial technology solutions, and assess potential risks; and (b) applied supervisory technology solutions to streamline its functions to make regulatory reporting of supervised financial institutions easier and more efficient; and (ii) through DTI, implemented the development of a range of financial technology innovations including those that specifically address women-led unserved or underserved MSMEs due to constraints in access to financial services from formal financial institutions. (IA: BSP, DTI) Target date: 2023-03-31
Action 4: The BSP: (i) issued on 26 April 2022 a joint circular and a memorandum of agreement with the DOF, the National Commission on Muslim Filipinos, and the Bangsamoro Government to create the Shari'ah Supervisory Board in Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao to promote Islamic finance and Islamic banking and finance in the region; and (ii) implemented a capacity building program on Islamic banking for over 700 representatives (with 62% women) of regulatory agencies, the banking industry, and other stakeholders. (IA: BSP) Target date: 2023-03-31
